note:
THE EVIDENCE MUST CONTAIN THE ASKER. That is the whole of this ticket, and it was found twice at two layers in one night. The retired predicate compared a source's mtime to the mtime in its .pyc header — both terms on disk, and a .pyc is SHARED, so any second interpreter in the same tree repairs the evidence without repairing the asking process. That second actor is not an edge case here; it is CC running proofs and doors in the very tree the daemon watches. Eleven green teeth stood over a live misattribution for exactly as long as no fixture used a real second interpreter.

THEN THE INSTRUMENT TURNED OUT TO HAVE THE PATIENT'S ILLNESS. loop_not_stale took its 'does this folder import cleanly?' reading in its own process, and its own process is the ground loop. It reproduced the stale loop's ImportError and read the misattribution as a real defect. The reading moved to a child seeded from this process's sys.path; two readings over one folder agree on a real defect and disagree on a stale loop.

WHAT THE VERDICT COST, and it is the part worth reading in a year: three of the eight criteria named an instrument that could not have shown what it claimed, and each was replaced rather than reported around. (2) a text grep for 'mtime'/'ImportError' returns 16 and 5 — from the module's own PROSE explaining which face a difference corresponds to, and from the retired comparison deliberately kept as reported-but-not-deciding payload; the instrument that works AST-walks the six deciding functions and asserts the banned spellings are not among the identifiers they touch. (4) reverting the predicate leaves test_discovery GREEN, because the prove-apart pair INJECTS the staleness answer — the deciding branch in loop.py had to be mutated instead (if False: 4 red, if True: 8 red, disjoint). (1) `git stash` cannot make the HEAD-red tooth fail rather than error, because HEAD has no read_all at all. A criterion measured by an instrument that cannot bite is a hollow green, and Law 8 says a false green is worse here than a red.

WHAT DID NOT CLOSE. The standing trouble ground-loop-device-survey is still OPEN, count 1, cleared_by []. A fixed predicate cannot reach an already-benched device — the folder is not even opened while the bench stands, and only TroubleDevice.clear() exits — and the process holding the wrong reading is the one that has to be replaced. It waits on a restart of pid 973171, which is Akien's to perform. This build changes the NEXT misattribution, not this one, and says so rather than letting the trouble look self-clearing.

AND 24% OF HELD OBJECTS READ UNDECIDABLE — 364 of 1497 over 172 modules, against a hypothesis that predicted 'a small, enumerable set'. It costs reach, not correctness (UNDECIDABLE never reads CURRENT), and the honest form of the miss is the number being printed in the coverage tally rather than the adjective being kept in the prose.
